content.text: Gathered Whispers, a Dark Gift feat, gives you some magical utility options and scaling parry Reaction to protect you from attacks. The feat provides no offensive benefits, and it doesn’t give you anything to build around, but it’s reasonably easy to add to any build that’s decent at Wisdom saves.

Gathered Whispers isn’t as powerful or flashy as many of the other Dark Gifts, but its drawback is also much less punishing. Because it calls for a Wisdom save and penalizes Ability Checks and Attack Rolls on a failure, the best users of Gathered Whispers are spellcasters, especially those who can’t cast Shield like the Cleric and the Druid. Paladins and Rangers will also find this very useful, especially if you’re building for melee.
Not especially powerful, but very fun. Augury is one of my favorite spells, and this lets you cast it right from level 1.
A parry similar to the Shield spell. It’s certianly powerful, but the uses and the bonus both match your Proficiency Bonus, so its benefits will scale slowly over time.

Annoying, but survivable. Being Deafened is a minor inconvenience, especially for such a short amount of time. Disadvantage on Ability Checks and Attacks Rolls are bigger problems, but if you can rely on abilities that force saving throws or avoid attacking in some other way, even that isn’t a big problem.

sections.heading: How Does the Natural 1 Mechanic Work For Dark Gift Feats?

content.text: It’s not totally clear how the natural 1 mechanic interacts with reroll mechanics like the Halfling’s Lucky feature or with Advantage/Disadvantage. Dark Gifts’ drawbacks trigger “Immediately after you make a D20 Test and roll a 1 on the d20.” How your DM interprets this text can make Dark Gifts dramatically more or less risky.

The intent may be that you only care about the final d20 result. If you roll with Advantage and get a natural 1 on one die, you only care about the d20 that you keep. If this is the case, you can protect yourself with the Halfling’s Lucky feature or by using Heroic Inspiration to reroll. Of course, that makes Dark Gift feats only threatening if you don’t have Heroic Inspiration to rescue you.

If the intent is instead that you trigger the effect if you roll a natural 1 on any d20 rolled during the test, rerolls, Advantage, and Disadvantage all become terrifying risks because they now increase your odds of triggering the save. And can you be forced to save multiple times on one D20 Test?
I think the intent is that you look at the final result after rerolls, etc., because the game treats you as having rolled that number. But check with your DM about how they plan to interpet the text.
